strengths: Sound is local by rule and the two carriers are narrow: the socket road plays only for a GM sender and only on the addressed user (sfx.mjs:100-105), the card road is held to the card's own readers, a veiled card is silent where its words never arrive (sfx.mjs:127-133), and a player's card cannot reach the GMs or play the volume-ignoring siren unless the document itself carries the safeword marker (sfx-play.mjs:719-737).

A death the GMs keep is sounded by address, never as a flag every console would receive (sfx-play.mjs:530-549, death.mjs:298-301); a Truth Bullet's and a Level Up's sound go to every owner by address (sfx-play.mjs:516-528, E59 B-S4).

The autoplay lock is handled as measured: a locked browser drops and counts the sound instead of queueing it (sfx-play.mjs:580-583), and Test refuses before a load that would never settle (sfx-play.mjs:785-790).

World-state sounds fire on edges, read against a baseline taken at ready, so a reload mid-trial or mid-turn announces nothing (sfx.mjs:217-230, floorSounds 280-306, pure and tested by R7106 by its own note).

The music engine marks its own writes with a depth counter rather than a boolean (music-play.mjs:52-76), chains every apply (371-379), checks an interruption against the documents before trusting its record (409-413, 898-912), and gives a mapping change by any GM to whichever GM is primary when the settle ends (109-161).
The map saves one key at a time through one chain, keeps another GM's choice of a third playlist and repairs only the race it is for (music-states.mjs:289-395).

The murder music never touches a world document: one track by AudioHelper on the participants' and GMs' browsers, the room's music held locally (murder-music.mjs:27-60), so a bystander's playlists and HUD do not change.

float-text.mjs runs no frame loop: it follows the placeholder on mutations, resizes and scrolls only, one frame at most per burst, counted (float-text.mjs:239-293); every read before the first write (154-161).

transitions.mjs writes nothing, plays nothing under reduced motion or with the table's switch off, and cuts rather than queues a second flash table (transitions.mjs:187, 204-216); its onsets hold to three a second (flashRate).

findings.title: Play and Stop the track are open to every GM while the music's record lives on the primary: an assistant GM's Play leaves the primary's record empty, and an assistant GM's Stop the track during the body's silence brings the music back into it
findings.where: scripts/music-play.mjs:1098-1102 and 1179-1183 (any GM), 175 and 178 (interrupted, silenced: one browser's memory), 381-388 (enabled: primary only), 932-993 (the primary's watcher), 1206-1222 (Reset's give-back); scripts/sound-panel.mjs:362 (the window's only gate is isGM)
findings.what_happens: playTrack and resetMusic test game.user.isGM only. On an assistant GM, playTrack pauses every playing playlist with the HELD flag and records `interrupted` there; on the primary the same writes arrive with ourDoing() false, the pauses are ignored (onManualEnd: not its sound), and the cue's start makes onManualStart record held [] because nothing is still playing. When the state then moves, the primary lets go of nothing the assistant flagged (448-454), and when the GM stops the cue the primary resumes nothing. Separately: while the body's silence holds (silenced on the primary, set at 471-472), an assistant GM's Stop the track runs resetMusic with no record: nothing is playing, so it resumes every HELD playlist (1211-1217), and its schedule() does nothing because it is not the primary; the primary's playingState is still bodyFound, so nothing re-silences, and the afternoon plays through the silence the owner's D8 chose. The primary pressing the same button re-silences at once (1187-1190, 1222).
findings.failure_scenario: Two GMs; a body is announced and the room goes silent; the assistant GM opens the Sound window and presses Stop the track to clear a cue: the afternoon playlist fades back in for the whole table over the discovery and stays.
findings.expected: One client decides (music.mjs:40-45 says so): Play and Stop the track carried out on the primary, or refused on another GM with the primary's name, as the 1.2.42 fix proposed.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a forward to the primary: sound-panel.mjs:276-288 calls playTrack/resetMusic directly and neither asks the bridge; no socket in music-play.mjs (the header says none). Looked for the primary re-checking after another GM's playlist writes: watchManualPlayback ignores sounds of mapped playlists (943), so the resumed afternoon (a mapped playlist) wakes nothing, and no updatePlaylist handler calls schedule. The silence's own record cannot be read by the assistant (a module variable). The Sound window is the GM panel's tile for every GM (gm-panel.mjs:207).
findings.tests_near: none found that calls playTrack or resetMusic from a second GM (old-1.2.42-comms.json COMM-10 says the same); scenario 87 parts C1-C4 drive a second GM's map write, not Play or Reset
findings.live_check: new live check: two GMs, Music follows on, a body announced with nothing mapped to it; the assistant presses Stop the track; listen on a player for 30 s.

findings.title: A GM who becomes the primary takes over no running cue and no silence: the next state change plays its playlist over a cue still on repeat, and the old holds stay flagged
findings.where: scripts/music-play.mjs:264-283 (adoptRunningInterruption at ready only), 305-335, 397-503 (apply), 520-564 (crossfade stops only the map's playlists)
findings.what_happens: interrupted, silenced and playingState are module variables of the primary's tab. A second GM's ready ran adoptRunningInterruption while it was not the primary, where `enabled()` is false and it returns (306). Nothing in the music family listens for the primary changing (no userConnected or drpgPrimaryReady hook in music-play.mjs, by grep). So after the primary leaves, the new primary holds no record: on the next state change apply sees no interruption, and crossfade stops only `ours()` (the mapped playlists) and starts the new one, while the GM's cue in Situational plays on with repeat set (1140). The playlists the cue or the silence held keep HELD true (cleared only for `next`), and a later Stop the track into silence resumes them.
findings.failure_scenario: The primary GM puts a cue on and then drops from the session; the assistant GM advances to Evening: the Evening playlist starts under the cue and both play for the table until someone presses Stop the track.
findings.expected: The GM who becomes the primary reads the running interruption and the holds from the world (adoptRunningInterruption already does this from documents) before its first apply.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked whether schedule or apply adopts on the fly: apply only clears an interruption that has stopped (409-413), it never builds one. Checked whether the map-settle fix (E50 FG1, 109-116) covers it: it covers a mapping change within the settle, not a cue or a silence. isPrimaryGm is recomputed per call (utils.mjs:458-462), so the new GM does drive the next apply. LIVE-E50-04 names a real GM leaving within the map settle only.
findings.live_check: new live check: two GMs; GM A (primary) plays a cue from the Sound window over a mapped Afternoon; A closes the tab; GM B advances the hour; listen on a player.

findings.title: With Music follows the game state off (the default), a cue stopped from Foundry's Playlists sidebar leaves the music it paused paused and flagged
findings.where: scripts/music-play.mjs:1006-1021 (watchManualEnd returns on !enabled()), 932-956, 1082-1087 (the note that Play works with the switch off), 1132 (holdEverything); scripts/settings.mjs:2004-2018 (default false)
findings.what_happens: playTrack does its own bookkeeping so that Play and Stop the track work with the switch off (1082-1087): it pauses every playing playlist with the HELD flag. The road back for a cue stopped any other way is watchManualEnd, which returns at once when enabled() is false. A GM who stops the cue where Foundry puts the stop button, in the Playlists sidebar, gets silence: the playlist they had on stays paused with HELD true and `interrupted` stays set until Stop the track is pressed. The Play tab's line says 'Stop it, and the music that was playing before comes back.'
findings.failure_scenario: A GM who never turned the switch on plays a cue over their own ambient playlist from the Sound window, later stops the cue in the Playlists sidebar, and the room stays silent; the ambient has to be restarted by hand.
findings.expected: The cue's end gives back what Play held whether or not the state machine is on, or the line says that only Stop the track gives it back.
findings.refutation_tried: The label of the Reset button is 'Stop the track' (en.json DRPG.Music.reset), so 'Stop it' may mean that button; the sentence still promises the music back on a stop, and the sidebar's stop is the natural one. Checked that no other hook resumes: resumeAmbient has three callers (1019, 1029 and the record), all behind enabled().
findings.live_check: one GM, switch off: play a sidebar playlist, Play a cue from the Sound window, stop the cue from the sidebar.

findings.title: The season reset rings the Monocub sound on every GM and on each cub's player, once per Monocub it clears
findings.what_happens: onActorFlagged plays 'monocub' on every updateActor whose changes carry the monocub flag, for every GM and the actor's owners. The season reset clears each cub with setMonocub(actor, false, { quiet: true }); `quiet` silences the toast only, and the flag write reaches the hook like any other, so a reset of a season with three Monocubs plays the sound up to three times on each GM (the 80 ms cooldown merges only writes closer than that).
findings.failure_scenario: The GM runs the season reset at the end of a campaign arc and hears the Monocub chime two or three times in the middle of the reset's own report.
findings.expected: A quiet change of the mark (the reset, a revive's quiet road at gm-students.mjs:649) sounds nothing, as it toasts nothing.
findings.refutation_tried: The catalogue's hint says the sound plays when a student 'stops being one', which covers a GM's revive; it says nothing of the reset. Looked for a guard on the reset (a hold of the sound engine during runSteps): none in sfx.mjs or season-wipe.mjs 448-460.

findings.title: A text field that floats over the case map at a zoom other than 1 is drawn at the unzoomed font in a zoomed box
findings.where: scripts/float-text.mjs:57-66 (FACE copies font-size, padding and borders), 150-188 (lift: the box is the screen's, the face the computed style's)
findings.what_happens: lift() places the field in the top layer at its box on the screen (getBoundingClientRect, which includes the case map camera's CSS transform) and copies its face from getComputedStyle, whose font-size, padding and border widths are the untransformed values. The comment at 165-170 says the top layer is reached by no transform. At zoom 0.5 the floating field is half as wide as the field's layout but its text is drawn at full size, so it wraps twice as often and grows taller; at zoom 2 the text is half the size it showed a moment before. The owner-116 fix (holdSize) set the placeholder right; the face was not scaled.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM zoomed out on the case map clicks a node's note: the note jumps to twice its type size inside a field half as wide, and shrinks back when they click away.
findings.expected: The floating field keeps the size the text had on the screen (the face scaled by the box's ratio to the layout size, which holdSize already computes).
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that window scaling is not a transform (window-scale.mjs scaleWindow goes through setPosition), so only transformed ancestors such as the case map's canvas are touched. audit/float-sweep.mjs I7 (lines 360-400) measures the floating box and the placeholder at zoom 0.5 and 2, not the font. Not run here.
findings.live_check: Chromium (class C): audit/float-sweep.mjs's I7 capture with the floating field's computed font-size compared to the field's own font-size times the zoom.

findings.title: Every button sound still waits 120 ms to see whether a window sound beats it; the number the comment says E17 tunes by ear is unchanged
findings.what_happens: windowButton and sheetButton yield to windowOpen and windowClose, so with a file mapped each press's sound is held 120 ms on a timer and then played unless a window sound cancels it. The sound of every press lands 120 ms after the press. The comment still reads 'E17 is where that happens', a stage long shipped; config.mjs:5012 says 'Tuned by ear in E17, alongside YIELD_MS'. No reading of that tuning was found.
findings.failure_scenario: A player clicking through the sheet's pips hears each click a beat after the press, which reads as the interface lagging.
findings.expected: A recorded reading of the delay at a table, or a shorter hold for presses that open no window.
findings.refutation_tried: The hold is deliberate and documented (60-69); the press itself is not delayed, only its sound. Whether 120 ms is heard as lag is a table's question, so the severity rests on the old report's word, not a reading.
